### finnertallon-png/contract-deadline-agent
- URL: https://github.com/finnertallon-png/contract-deadline-agent
- Exact commit / revision: `c891f5ff391abc58b874675783a7ff2c3775c7bb`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: strong / Master contender
- What it contains: MIT construction/commercial contract deadline engine that extracts notice provisions, cure periods and time-bound obligations, stores provenance, separates trigger-plus-duration from calendar dates, routes low-confidence clauses to review, writes structured outputs and reconciles human-entered trigger dates into Outlook reminders. Tests prove strict date parsing, relative-date arithmetic, idempotent event reconciliation, trigger-date changes and explicit refusal of unsupported business-day calculations.
- Rare or undernoticed value: It addresses a different but financially decisive part of change recovery: a technically valid change can become unrecoverable if notice/claim timing is missed. The project deliberately refuses ambiguous dates instead of inventing legal-operational certainty.
- Likely buyer / user: General contractors, specialty subcontractors, claims/change teams, commercial managers and project-controls groups.
- Painful problem: Change entitlement leaks because notice clauses, cure windows and priced-claim deadlines are buried in contracts and become actionable only after a project event occurs.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price change-notice preservation audit: ingest one contract plus the active change/RFI log and deliver a human-reviewed notice/deadline matrix with calendar reminders; recurring per-project monitoring after validation.
- Build-time / data advantage: High; compresses roughly 2-4+ months of contract-clause extraction, M365/SharePoint/Outlook plumbing, review states, date/refusal rules and reconciliation behavior.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; `README.md`; `docs/LIMITATIONS.md`; source/test tree; `tests/test_outlook.py` proving absolute-date rejection, trigger-relative due dates, unsupported business-day refusal, update/delete/idempotency behavior; root MIT `LICENSE`.
- License / rights: MIT verified. Contract documents/customer data retain their own confidentiality and access constraints; outputs are operational review aids, not legal advice.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT, with legal/compliance review for production claims workflows.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Low-profile repo positioned as a deadline agent, but its fail-closed timing semantics are exactly the claim-preservation layer most drawing-change tools omit.
- Value score: **29/30** — A4, B5, C5, D5, E5, F5. High ceiling because preserving one missed high-value claim can justify substantial spend; evidence and rights are unusually strong.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal revision/quantity evidence -> RFI Evidence Ledger entitlement citation -> this contract-notice engine -> human trigger confirmation -> notice/claim deadline calendar -> Massing/Procore-style RFI/change workflow.
- Next action: Add versioned amendment/change-order supersession so later documents can modify baseline notice rules without silently retaining stale deadlines; then benchmark on held-out construction contracts.

### Sunrise-Systems/contractor-toolkit
- URL: https://github.com/Sunrise-Systems/contractor-toolkit
- Exact commit / revision: `44fb0994ca176a1bf6657af254d7556e8b351bdc`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Status: watch
- What it contains: MIT contractor workflow/skill pack covering ROM and conceptual estimates, formal bids, plan takeoff guidance, scope checks, subcontractor bid packages/leveling, contracts, RFIs, submittals, change orders, T&M, daily logs and progress pay applications. The repository includes deterministic validation scripts/tests and project-bound estimating state/provenance patterns, while its own documentation admits several integrations/reviews remain incomplete.
- Rare or undernoticed value: A broad, low-attention corpus of contractor artifact/state expectations that can accelerate product/workflow design even though it is not a substitute for OpenTakeoff or ScopeSignal's evidence engines.
- Likely buyer / user: Small/midsize GCs and specialty contractors adopting AI-assisted preconstruction/project administration.
- Painful problem: Generic agents produce attractive but operationally unsafe construction documents without project state, provenance, issuance controls or consistent downstream artifacts.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Use only the validated artifact/state patterns behind a ScopeSignal-generated RFI/CO packet or as a contractor document-production assistant; paid wedge would be a fixed-price workflow implementation, not sale of the template corpus itself.
- Build-time / data advantage: Medium-high for workflow/document design; likely saves 1-2+ months of domain UX/artifact mapping, but much less on geometry or entitlement logic.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; root tree; `README.md`; validation/test directories and estimating/document plugin structure; root `LICENSE`. Documentation explicitly distinguishes deterministic validation from skills that remain guidance-only and notes supervised domain review/PDF verification gaps.
- License / rights: MIT verified for repository code/content; downstream generated documents still require project-specific professional review.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT terms, but treat domain guidance as unvalidated until independently tested.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Zero/low-attention contractor plugin packaging hides an unusually broad construction artifact map.
- Value score: **23/30** — A4, B3, C4, D3, E4, F5. Useful accelerator, but not rare enough or complete enough to displace existing ScopeSignal leaders.
- Combination opportunities: Feed evidence-backed ScopeSignal findings into deterministic RFI/CO/T&M/pay-app artifact generation while preserving source IDs and human approval.
- Next action: Extract only objectively testable state/provenance guardrails and compare generated CO/RFI artifacts against experienced contractor review before product use.

- Reuse classification: Inspect/learn/clean-room only unless permission/license is established.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Tiny/low-attention project whose valuable asset is evidence provenance and opportunity identity, not the crawler itself.
- Value score: **21/30** — A4, B4, C4, D4, E4, F1. Rights are the main limiter.
- Combination opportunities: Urban Signal + Accela/Revitalize collectors -> canonical property/entity resolver -> independently built PermitSignal-style evidence object -> trade-specific PermitPlate opportunity scoring.
- Next action: Recreate the evidence-object contract independently and compare precision/duplicate suppression against current PermitPlate lead rows; do not copy code without permission.

- Painful problem: Parcel/project research is often a folder of links and screenshots with no explicit completeness state, reviewer accountability or evidence gaps.

- Build-time / data advantage: Medium; compresses evidence schema, completeness rules, import validation and report UX by several weeks to a few months.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; `README.md`; recursive tree with tests/source/privacy/limitations docs; MIT `LICENSE`; project/analysis tests and official-source structure.
- License / rights: MIT verified for repository code; underlying municipal/property records retain source-specific terms and privacy constraints.
- Reuse classification: Directly reusable under MIT, with source/data rights reviewed independently.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Low-attention local diligence tool whose standout feature is fail-closed evidence completeness rather than GIS visualization.
- Value score: **23/30** — A3, B4, C4, D3, E4, F5. Useful evidence layer but overlaps existing property-intelligence leaders and is partly manual.
- Combination opportunities: PermitPlate permit -> canonical parcel -> official source bundle -> ParcelProof-style completeness/conflict state -> opportunity/value score.
- Next action: Automate official PermitPlate source retrieval into this evidence model and measure how often a candidate parcel can reach a defensible complete state without manual research.

### Beveren-Software-Inc/Field_Service_Management
- URL: https://github.com/Beveren-Software-Inc/Field_Service_Management
- Exact commit / revision: `ab6d56d1069882326475f256d09cc63236eddec1`

- What it contains: Substantial ERPNext/Frappe field-service system with the lifecycle Service Request -> optional Service Quotation -> Service Order -> Service Appointments -> work execution -> Sales Invoice, plus scheduling/dispatch, technician/skills, parts/inventory, repairs and an Annual Maintenance Contract model. The AMC schema explicitly stores contract total, service budget, spare-parts budget, utilized service/spares and the linked service order; a dashboard card counts service appointments where `per_billed = 0`.

- Likely buyer / user: HVAC, electrical, fire/life-safety, mechanical, appliance and outsourced facilities service firms using recurring service contracts.
- Painful problem: Revenue and margin leak when completed service is unbilled, noncontract work is incorrectly absorbed into an AMC, or service/parts utilization outruns contract economics.
- Monetization mechanism / first paid wedge: Fixed-price service-revenue-leakage diagnostic: import service orders/appointments/contracts/invoices and flag completed-unbilled work, entitlement mismatches and contract budget overrun; recurring audit after proof.
- Build-time / data advantage: Very high; compresses months of service-order, contract, billing, technician, inventory and dispatch domain plumbing.
- Concrete evidence inspected: Exact revision; recursive tree; `README.md`; `beveren_fsm/field_service_management/doctype/amc_contract/amc_contract.json` showing total/service/spares budgets and utilized amounts; `number_card/non_billed_appointments/non_billed_appointments.json` explicitly filtering `Service Appointment.per_billed = 0`; large `service_order.py`/schema plus Sales Invoice customizations; root `license.txt`.
- License / rights: AGPL-3.0 verified. Proprietary SaaS embedding requires deliberate AGPL architecture/compliance; ERPNext/Frappe dependency terms also require review.
- Reuse classification: Reusable under AGPL obligations; otherwise use as an architecture/domain reference or keep a proprietary analytics layer separate from covered code with legal review.
- Why it is not already obvious / crowded: Low-profile field-service repo whose AMC utilization + explicit unbilled-appointment surface expose a dollar-recovery wedge hidden inside general FSM functionality.
- Value score: **25/30** — A4, B4, C5, D4, E5, F3. Copyleft is the principal deduction.
- Combination opportunities: CMMS Normalize for heterogeneous imports + Beveren entitlement/billing model + FM-DispatchBench technician optimization + JpAbg/CAFM warranty/service-contract rules -> facilities service leakage and dispatch intelligence stack.
- Next action: Build a read-only benchmark query mapping completed appointment -> AMC coverage/budget -> service/parts usage -> invoice existence, then quantify recoverable leakage on synthetic or customer-authorized exports.
